evidence.observation: The IMO listed 120 highlighted confirmed maritime incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and wider Middle East cumulatively as of October 22, not 120 in October alone.

Lloyd’s List counted 104 non-Iranian-linked transits through Hormuz in October 5–11 versus 126 in September 28–October 4, a 17% weekly decline, although this cohort remained 31% above the August weekly average.

British government communiqué documents the eight-minister meeting and endorsement of dialogue and de-escalation. Signed diplomatic language is advocacy, not an implemented ceasefire, and republications by the same signatories are not independent.

Turkish foreign-ministry official communiqué is the upstream policy statement for the Istanbul meeting. The direct HTML exposed no visible paragraphs under the repository parser; do not cite it as a raw original-body witness.

Yemeni government agency article was located as the alleged transport-ministry upstream statement on Aden airport. The direct HTML returned only navigation/shell text despite HTTP 200, so no original-body claim or impact was admitted.

Anadolu described Yemeni official missile allegations and correspondent-heard explosions in Aden. No independent ballistic identification, verified launch position or damage assessment was obtained from that report.

followup.counterevidence_findings: The CTP risk assessment and persistent maritime incidents show no completed ceasefire; urging diplomacy cannot be equated with stopping attacks.
followup.limitations: No authentic agreement signed by Iran and the US or demonstrated free shipping; held as contextual stabilizing diplomacy rather than counted as an implemented event. The performed_at timestamp marks completion of this bounded follow-up by the actual logged cutoff, not the time of an individual query.
followup.reporting_chain: Guardian reported the summit; UK and Turkish websites reproduce a single collectively authored governmental diplomatic statement.
